meta.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy risk at diagnosis (children)
meta.authors: Kwon O, Nam YS, Kim HJ, Yeh HR, Kim MJ, Lee YJ, Kim E, Lee EH, You SJ, Ko TS, Yum MS
meta.outcome: Probability that a child with newly diagnosed epilepsy develops drug-resistant epilepsy, from eight features known at diagnosis.
meta.clinical_utility: Risk stratification at the first epilepsy diagnosis: earlier referral to a specialist centre, closer follow-up and earlier consideration of advanced therapy for high-risk children. Single-centre model with internal validation only.

source_link.label: original tool
source_link.title: Pediatric DRE Risk Calculator (Kwon, Asan Medical Center)

meta.cff_info:
What this shows. The probability that a child with newly diagnosed epilepsy will develop drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) — failure of two appropriate antiseizure medications to achieve one year of seizure freedom, per the ILAE definition — estimated from eight features available at diagnosis (Kwon et al., Seizure 2026).

Cohort. Single tertiary centre (Asan Medical Center, Seoul), 4208 children aged 0–18 years diagnosed 1995–2017 and followed to 2024; 1419 (33.7%) developed DRE. Predictors were selected by LASSO and fitted by multivariable logistic regression, with a random 70/30 training–validation split.

Performance. Area under the ROC curve 0.765 (95% CI 0.747–0.783) in training and 0.778 (0.751–0.805) in the held-out validation set; optimism-corrected 0.761 after 1000 bootstrap resamples. Calibration was good (calibration-in-the-large −0.010, slope 1.062; Brier 0.176). At the Youden threshold, sensitivity was 0.63 and specificity 0.78, with a positive predictive value of 0.59.

Limits. No external validation — the validation set is a random split of the same centre's data, so this is internal validation only. The centre is a tertiary referral hospital, where 33.7% had DRE against 20–30% in population studies, so risks here are likely higher than in general practice. Medication choice and sequence were deliberately left out, so the estimate is a baseline risk at diagnosis, not a treatment-response prediction. The absence of a documented finding was treated as absence of that finding.

Original tool. The authors publish their own calculator at amc-ped.github.io/DRE_calculator (Ohcheol Kwon, Asan Medical Center Children's Hospital). This page reproduces the published model and matches the paper's worked example (76.2%).

predictors.name: Seizure onset before 1 year of age
predictors.assess: Age at first seizure below 12 months (OR 1.91).

predictors.name: Seizure frequency before treatment

options.label: Monthly (at least monthly, less than weekly)
Weekly (at least weekly, less than daily)

predictors.assess: Pretreatment seizure frequency — the strongest predictor in the model (daily OR 4.28, weekly 3.40, monthly 1.93 versus yearly).

predictors.name: History of status epilepticus
predictors.assess: Continuous seizure activity ≥5 min, or recurrent seizures without recovery of consciousness, before the epilepsy diagnosis (OR 2.07).

predictors.name: Developmental disorders
predictors.assess: Documented developmental delay or intellectual disability present before the epilepsy diagnosis (OR 1.91).

predictors.name: Neurological abnormalities on examination
predictors.assess: Focal deficits, abnormal tone, pathological reflexes or cranial nerve abnormalities at diagnosis (OR 1.37).

predictors.name: Epilepsy type
predictors.assess: ILAE 2017 epilepsy type. Combined generalized and focal epilepsy carries the highest risk (OR 2.21 versus generalized).

predictors.name: Structural aetiology
predictors.assess: A brain MRI abnormality judged causally related to the epilepsy (OR 2.09). Aetiology categories are not mutually exclusive, so structural and infectious/immune can both be selected.

predictors.name: Infectious or immune aetiology
predictors.assess: Epilepsy attributed to a documented CNS infection or an immune-mediated process (OR 2.29).

model.note: Single-centre tertiary-referral cohort (n=4208) with internal validation only (random 70/30 split, AUC 0.778; optimism-corrected 0.761). DRE was 33.7% in this centre against 20–30% in population studies, so absolute risks are probably higher than in general practice. The model describes risk at diagnosis and does not account for which medication is chosen.
model.viz_info: The donut shows the predicted probability of drug-resistant epilepsy. The waterfall starts from a baseline child (yearly seizures, generalized epilepsy, no other feature) and shows how each feature raises that probability; the model is additive on the log-odds scale, so the steps are not simple percentage additions.

provenance.source: Kwon et al., Seizure 2026;142:8–17 (doi 10.1016/j.seizure.2026.07.021, PMID 42585883). Odds ratios from Table 2A / Results 2.5.2; performance from Results 2.5.3 and Fig. 3; worked example from the Fig. 2 nomogram caption. Coefficient values cross-checked against the authors' own calculator (https://amc-ped.github.io/DRE_calculator/, no licence file — nothing copied).
provenance.notes: Logistic model: p = 1/(1+exp(-(intercept + Σβx))). Every β matches its published OR to <0.011. The intercept (-2.1437) is the value stated in the authors' own calculator; the paper's worked example (logit(0.762) - Σβ for onset<1y + weekly + developmental + combined) independently gives -2.1446, agreeing to within 0.001 (rounding of the printed 76.2%, worth 0.02 pp). build_kwon_peds_dre.py asserts both. Aetiology enters as two separate binary indicators (present vs absent), as in the paper. Set review_status to human_reviewed after a person reproduces the worked example on the live page.
